options: No, 1 is neither prime nor composite
Yes, because it has one factor
questions.hint: 1 is a special number. It is neither prime nor composite because it has only one factor, itself.

questions.subject: maths
questions.question: Which of these is the smallest composite number?
questions.hint: 4 is the smallest composite number. It has factors 1, 2, and 4.

questions.subject: maths
questions.question: What is prime factorization?
options: Adding all the factors of a number
Writing a number as a product of its prime factors
Finding the square root of a number
Listing all even numbers less than a number
questions.hint: Prime factorization means expressing a number as a product of only its prime factors.

questions.subject: maths
questions.question: What is the prime factorization of 36?
questions.hint: 36 = 2 x 2 x 3 x 3, using only prime numbers. Writing it as 4 x 9 is not correct, since 4 and 9 are not prime.

questions.subject: maths
questions.question: What is the prime factorization of 60?
questions.hint: 60 = 2 x 2 x 3 x 5, breaking it down completely into prime numbers.

questions.subject: maths
questions.question: Which method is commonly used to find the prime factorization of a number?
questions.hint: The factor tree method breaks a number down step by step into its prime factors.

questions.subject: maths
questions.question: What is the prime factorization of 100?
questions.hint: 100 = 2 x 2 x 5 x 5, using only the prime numbers 2 and 5.

questions.subject: maths
questions.question: A number is divisible by 2 if:
options: It ends in an odd number
The sum of its digits is even
questions.hint: A number is divisible by 2 if its last digit is even, that is 0, 2, 4, 6, or 8.

questions.subject: maths
questions.question: A number is divisible by 5 if:
options: The sum of its digits is 5
questions.hint: A number is divisible by 5 if its last digit is 0 or 5.

questions.subject: maths
questions.question: A number is divisible by 4 if:
options: The sum of its digits is divisible by 4
The number formed by its last two digits is divisible by 4
questions.hint: A number is divisible by 4 if the number formed by its last two digits is divisible by 4. For example, 316 is divisible by 4 because 16 is divisible by 4.

questions.subject: maths
questions.question: A number is divisible by 8 if:
options: It is divisible by 2 and 4 separately
The number formed by its last three digits is divisible by 8
Its digit sum is divisible by 8
questions.hint: A number is divisible by 8 if the number formed by its last three digits is divisible by 8. For example, 1240 is divisible by 8 because 240 is divisible by 8.

questions.subject: maths
questions.question: Which of these numbers is divisible by both 4 and 8?
questions.hint: 248 is divisible by 8, since 248 divided by 8 equals 31, and any number divisible by 8 is also divisible by 4.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: Which two cities are considered the major sites of the Harappan Civilization?
questions.hint: Harappa and Mohenjodaro are the two best known major cities of the Harappan Civilization.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: In which present-day country are the cities of Harappa and Mohenjodaro located?
questions.hint: Both Harappa and Mohenjodaro are located in present-day Pakistan.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: What is the Great Bath, found at Mohenjodaro?
options: A water tank for washing clothes only
A large rectangular tank, likely used for ritual bathing
A modern bathroom built later by another civilization
questions.hint: The Great Bath is a large rectangular tank at Mohenjodaro, thought to have been used for ritual or religious bathing.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: What material was used to make the Great Bath waterproof?
questions.hint: The Great Bath was lined with bitumen, a tar-like substance, to make it waterproof.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: Harappan cities were typically divided into which two parts?
options: The citadel and the lower town
questions.hint: Harappan cities were generally divided into a raised citadel and a larger lower town.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: Which part of a Harappan city usually contained large public buildings?
questions.hint: The citadel, a raised and often walled area, usually held large public buildings.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: Which part of a Harappan city was mainly residential?
questions.hint: The lower town was the larger, mainly residential part of a Harappan city.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: What is notable about the layout of streets in Harappan cities?
options: They were laid out in a grid pattern, crossing at right angles
They were built only in circles
They were narrow winding lanes with no pattern
There were no streets at all
questions.hint: Harappan streets were laid out in a grid pattern, crossing each other at right angles.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: What material were most Harappan buildings constructed from?
questions.hint: Most Harappan buildings were made from baked bricks.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: What was remarkable about the bricks used across the Harappan Civilization?
options: They were made only of glass
They were all painted bright colours
They followed a standard size ratio wherever they were made
They were never used for building walls
questions.hint: Harappan bricks followed a standard size ratio across many different sites, showing careful planning.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: What was the standard ratio of length to width to height commonly used for Harappan bricks?
questions.hint: Harappan bricks commonly followed a standard ratio of 4:2:1 for length, width, and height.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: What was likely the purpose of large granaries found in Harappan cities?
questions.hint: Granaries were large buildings likely used to store grain.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: Which Harappan city had a dockyard, suggesting a connection to sea trade?
questions.hint: Lothal had a dockyard, suggesting it was connected to maritime trade.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: In which present-day Indian state is Lothal located?
questions.hint: Lothal is located in the present-day Indian state of Gujarat.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: In which present-day Indian state is the Harappan site of Dholavira located?
questions.hint: Dholavira is located in the present-day Indian state of Gujarat.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: In which present-day Indian state is the Harappan site of Kalibangan located?
questions.hint: Kalibangan is located in the present-day Indian state of Rajasthan.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: What advanced feature did many Harappan houses have, connected to street drains?
questions.hint: Many Harappan houses had bathroom drains that connected to covered street drains.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: What does the advanced drainage system suggest about Harappan city planning?
options: The Harappans lived only in tents
The Harappans had no city planning at all
The Harappans placed great importance on cleanliness and sanitation
questions.hint: The advanced drainage system suggests that cleanliness and sanitation were important to the Harappans.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: Many Harappan houses were built around what central feature?
questions.hint: Many Harappan houses were built around a central courtyard.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: What did many Harappan houses have for their own water supply?
options: A river flowing through the house
Pipes bringing water from another city
A rainwater tank on the roof only
questions.hint: Many Harappan houses had their own well for water.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: What was one possible purpose of the massive walls around the citadel?
questions.hint: The massive citadel walls may have offered protection from floods or attacks.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: Which of these was a common feature of Harappan street drains?
options: They were covered with bricks or stone slabs
questions.hint: Harappan street drains were typically covered with bricks or stone slabs.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: Why do historians consider Harappan town planning to be advanced for its time?
options: Because they built only single houses with no city structure
Because their cities had no streets at all
Because they had electricity and modern plumbing
Because of features like grid streets, covered drains, and standardized bricks
questions.hint: Features like grid streets, covered drains, and standardized bricks show advanced town planning for their time.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: Which of these cities is NOT usually listed among the major Harappan sites?
questions.hint: Delhi is not usually listed among the major Harappan Civilization sites.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: What do archaeologists call the raised, walled part of a Harappan city?
questions.hint: Archaeologists call the raised, walled part of a Harappan city the citadel.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: Which of these best describes the general shape of most Harappan city streets?
options: Straight streets crossing each other at right angles
Streets that were built only underground
questions.hint: Most Harappan city streets were straight and crossed each other at right angles, forming a grid.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: What was one likely use of the Great Bath at Mohenjodaro?
options: For special ritual or religious bathing
questions.hint: The Great Bath was likely used for special ritual or religious bathing.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: Why might historians believe the Great Bath had a religious purpose?
options: Because ancient texts describe its exact religious use
Because it was found far away from any city
Because it had paintings of gods on its walls
Because bathing and cleanliness are often linked to rituals in many cultures
questions.hint: Historians link the Great Bath to religious ritual partly because bathing and cleanliness are connected to rituals in many cultures.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: What does the presence of granaries suggest about Harappan society?
options: They threw away all extra food
They imported all their food from other countries
They stored surplus grain, possibly for the whole community
questions.hint: Granaries suggest that surplus grain was stored, possibly for the benefit of the wider community.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: Which of these features shows careful city planning by the Harappans?
options: Cities built without any walls or boundaries
Random scattered huts with no pattern
Straight streets, covered drains, and standard-sized bricks
Streets that changed shape and size in every city
questions.hint: Straight streets, covered drains, and standard-sized bricks all point to careful, deliberate city planning.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: Approximately how many major and minor Harappan sites have been discovered so far?
questions.hint: Archaeologists have discovered over a thousand Harappan sites, both major and minor, across the region.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: Which of these cities is located in present-day India rather than Pakistan?
questions.hint: Lothal is located in present-day India, in the state of Gujarat, unlike Harappa and Mohenjodaro which are in Pakistan.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: What do archaeologists call the lower, more crowded part of a Harappan city?
questions.hint: Archaeologists call the lower, more crowded, mainly residential part of a Harappan city the lower town.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: Which of these was likely used to store surplus food in Harappan cities?
questions.hint: Granaries were likely used to store surplus food such as grain.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: What overall impression of Harappan society do the ruins of their cities give historians?
options: A disorganized society with no planning at all
A society with no interest in cleanliness
A well-organized society with careful planning and strong civic systems
A society that never built permanent structures
questions.hint: The ruins suggest a well-organized society with careful town planning and strong civic systems like drainage.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: Which crops did the Harappans commonly grow?
questions.hint: The Harappans commonly grew wheat and barley, along with other crops.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: The Harappans are considered among the earliest people in the world to grow which crop?
questions.hint: The Harappans are considered among the earliest people in the world to grow cotton.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: Which of these animals were kept by the Harappans?
questions.hint: The Harappans kept animals such as cattle, sheep, and goats.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: What era of tool-making does the Harappan Civilization belong to?
options: The Stone Age only, with no metal at all
questions.hint: The Harappan Civilization belongs to the Bronze Age, as they used bronze and copper tools.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: Which metals did the Harappans commonly use to make tools and objects?
questions.hint: The Harappans commonly used bronze and copper to make tools and objects.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: Which craft were the Harappans especially skilled at, using stones like carnelian?
questions.hint: The Harappans were especially skilled at bead making, using stones such as carnelian.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: What kind of pottery is commonly associated with the Harappans?
questions.hint: Painted black-on-red pottery is commonly associated with the Harappans.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: What evidence suggests the Harappans used ploughs for farming?
options: Modern tractors found buried at their sites
Terracotta plough models and a ploughed field found at archaeological sites
questions.hint: Terracotta plough models and traces of a ploughed field found by archaeologists suggest the Harappans used ploughs.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: Which material, used for jewellery, may have been traded from as far as Afghanistan?
questions.hint: Lapis lazuli, a blue stone used in jewellery, may have been traded from as far as Afghanistan.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: Which Harappan city's dockyard suggests strong maritime trade connections?
questions.hint: Lothal's dockyard suggests strong maritime trade connections for the Harappans.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: What were Harappan trade weights typically made from?
questions.hint: Harappan trade weights were typically made from chert, a hard type of stone.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: What shape were most Harappan trade weights?
questions.hint: Most Harappan trade weights were cubical in shape.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: Why were standardized weights important to Harappan trade?
options: They were used only by children as toys
They allowed accurate and fair measurement of goods
They were used only as decoration
They had no real purpose in daily life
questions.hint: Standardized weights allowed traders to measure goods accurately and fairly.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: Which distant civilization is believed to have had trade contact with the Harappans?
questions.hint: Mesopotamia is believed to have had trade contact with the Harappan Civilization.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: What evidence supports the idea that the Harappans traded with Mesopotamia?
options: There is no evidence at all connecting the two civilizations
Mesopotamian coins have been found with English writing on them
Harappan seals and objects have been found at Mesopotamian sites
Ancient photographs show Harappan ships in Mesopotamia
questions.hint: The discovery of Harappan seals and objects at Mesopotamian sites supports the idea of trade contact.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: Which of these materials were commonly used to make Harappan beads?
questions.hint: Harappan beads were commonly made from carnelian and other semi-precious stones.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: Why do many historians find it difficult to say whether the Harappans had kings?
options: Every Harappan site has a clearly labelled royal palace
No clear evidence of royal palaces or thrones has been found
Ancient records clearly name every Harappan king
Historians have never studied the Harappan Civilization
questions.hint: Historians find it difficult to confirm Harappan kingship because no clear evidence of royal palaces or thrones has been found.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: What famous small statue found at Mohenjodaro is often linked to a possible ruler or priest?
questions.hint: The small Priest-King statue found at Mohenjodaro is often linked to a possible ruler or priest figure.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: Which of these best describes Harappan farming tools, based on archaeological evidence?
options: Simple wooden ploughs, based on models and field marks found by archaeologists
No farming tools of any kind
Farming tools made entirely of glass
questions.hint: Archaeological evidence points to simple wooden ploughs, based on terracotta models and ploughed field marks.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: Which animals may have been used by the Harappans for transport?
options: Elephants only, based on strong evidence
Bullocks and possibly camels or donkeys
questions.hint: Bullocks, and possibly camels or donkeys, may have been used by the Harappans for transport.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: What do historians study to understand what the Harappans ate and farmed?
options: Remains of seeds, grains, and animal bones found at sites
Written cookbooks left behind by the Harappans
questions.hint: Historians study remains of seeds, grains, and animal bones found at archaeological sites to understand Harappan food and farming.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: Which of these was NOT a major Harappan craft?
questions.hint: Iron smelting was not a major Harappan craft, since they belonged to the Bronze Age and mainly used bronze and copper.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: Why is Harappan pottery useful to historians?
options: It has no historical value at all
It shows the artistic style and daily life of the people who made it
It was created after the civilization ended
questions.hint: Harappan pottery is useful because it reveals artistic style and details about daily life.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: What does the discovery of cotton seeds at Harappan sites suggest?
options: The Harappans grew and possibly wove cotton into cloth
Cotton was only used for building houses
The Harappans never used any plant fibres
Cotton was imported from a completely different, unrelated civilization far in the future
questions.hint: The discovery of cotton seeds suggests the Harappans grew cotton and likely wove it into cloth.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: Which of these is evidence of long-distance trade in the Harappan Civilization?
options: Modern shipping containers found at Harappan sites
Precious stones and materials found far from where they naturally occur
questions.hint: Finding precious stones and materials far from their natural source is evidence of long-distance trade.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: What do the standardized weights and bricks across Harappan sites suggest about their society?
options: There was likely some shared system of measurement and organization across the civilization
Weights and bricks were purely decorative, with no practical use
The Harappans never communicated between cities
Every Harappan city used completely different, unrelated systems
questions.hint: Standardized weights and bricks suggest a shared system of measurement and organization across Harappan society.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: Which of these animals is generally NOT believed to have been common in Harappan times, based on limited evidence?
questions.hint: Evidence for the horse in Harappan times is limited, unlike more common animals such as bulls, goats, and sheep.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: What do terracotta toys and figurines found at Harappan sites suggest?
options: Children may have played with toys, and craftspeople made small clay models
Toys were only used by adults for trade
Figurines were only used as building material
The Harappans never made any small objects
questions.hint: Terracotta toys and figurines suggest that children may have played with toys and that craftspeople made small clay models.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: Which of these best summarises the Harappan economy?
options: An economy based entirely on modern factories
An economy based only on hunting wild animals
An economy with no trade of any kind
A mix of farming, herding, craft-making, and trade over long distances
questions.hint: The Harappan economy was a mix of farming, herding, craft-making, and long-distance trade.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: Why do historians consider trade to have been important to Harappan cities?
options: Trade was banned in Harappan society
Cities needed materials that were not locally available, brought in through trade
Cities produced absolutely everything they needed locally
There is no evidence that Harappan cities ever traded with anyone
questions.hint: Trade was important because cities needed materials, like certain stones and metals, that were not available locally.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: What material were most Harappan seals made from?
questions.hint: Most Harappan seals were made from steatite, a soft stone, which was often glazed after carving.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: What shape were most Harappan seals?
options: Long and thin like a ruler
questions.hint: Most Harappan seals were square in shape.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: Why is it difficult for historians to read Harappan script today?
options: Historians have refused to study the script
The script was written in modern English letters
There are no surviving examples of the script
The script has not yet been deciphered
questions.hint: Historians find it difficult to read Harappan script because it has not yet been deciphered.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: Which animal appears most frequently on Harappan seals?
questions.hint: A unicorn-like single-horned animal is the most frequently depicted figure on Harappan seals.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: What was probably stamped or pressed using these seals?
options: Clay tags attached to goods, to mark ownership or trade
questions.hint: Seals were likely pressed onto clay tags attached to goods, to mark ownership or trade.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: Harappan seals have been found in which distant region, suggesting trade contact?
questions.hint: Harappan seals have been found in Mesopotamia, suggesting trade contact between the two regions.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: About how many different signs have been identified in the Harappan script?
questions.hint: Historians have identified about 400 different signs in the Harappan script.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: Which of these is NOT true about the Harappan script?
options: It is often found on seals
It has been fully translated by historians
questions.hint: The Harappan script has not been fully translated by historians; it remains undeciphered.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: What evidence would help historians decipher the Harappan script fastest?
options: A bilingual inscription, with the same message written in two known scripts
A new seal with no writing on it
A photograph of a Harappan person
questions.hint: A bilingual inscription, showing the same text in a known script, would help historians decipher the Harappan script much faster.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: What often appears on a Harappan seal along with the animal figure?
options: A short line of pictographic signs
questions.hint: A short line of pictographic signs often appears on a Harappan seal along with the animal figure.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: Which of these animals is commonly seen on Harappan seals besides the unicorn?
questions.hint: The humped bull is commonly seen on Harappan seals, along with other animals such as the unicorn.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: What do many historians believe seals were used for in Harappan trade?
options: To mark ownership of goods being transported
To write letters to family members
To pay taxes directly, like coins
To decorate the walls of houses only
questions.hint: Many historians believe seals were used to mark ownership of goods being transported in trade.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: Where were many Harappan seals discovered by archaeologists?
options: At city sites like Mohenjodaro and Harappa
Buried in countries outside Asia entirely
Only in modern museums with no digging involved
questions.hint: Many Harappan seals were discovered by archaeologists at city sites such as Mohenjodaro and Harappa.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: Which of these best describes the Harappan script?
options: A pictographic script that has not yet been deciphered
A script with no written signs at all
A fully modern alphabet used today
questions.hint: The Harappan script is a pictographic script that has not yet been deciphered.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: Why do many attempts to decipher the Harappan script remain unsuccessful?
options: The script is written in a modern European language
No historians have ever tried to study it
No one has found a bilingual text linking it to a known language
The script was destroyed and no examples survive
questions.hint: Attempts to decipher the script remain unsuccessful mainly because no bilingual text linking it to a known language has been found.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: What object often appears in front of the unicorn on Harappan seals?
options: A small stand, believed to be used for offerings
questions.hint: A small stand, believed to be an offering stand, often appears in front of the unicorn figure on seals.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: Which of these is a reason seals may have been important for trade?
options: They could show who owned or sent a shipment of goods
They replaced the need for any trade at all
They were used to cook food
questions.hint: Seals may have been important for trade because they could show who owned or sent a shipment of goods.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: How is Harappan writing typically arranged on seals?
options: In a short horizontal line above the animal figure
In a large paragraph covering the whole seal
It never appears with an animal figure
questions.hint: Harappan writing typically appears as a short horizontal line of signs above the animal figure on a seal.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: Which term describes writing using pictures or symbols instead of an alphabet?
questions.hint: Pictographic describes writing that uses pictures or symbols instead of an alphabet.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: What can studying seals tell historians about Harappan trade connections?
options: The exact price of every item traded
Which distant regions the Harappans may have traded with
The names of every trader involved
questions.hint: Studying where Harappan seals have been found can tell historians which distant regions the Harappans may have traded with.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: Which of these is true about the animals shown on Harappan seals?
options: No animals are ever shown on Harappan seals
They include real animals like bulls and elephants, and a mysterious unicorn-like creature
questions.hint: Harappan seals show real animals such as bulls and elephants, as well as a mysterious unicorn-like creature.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: Harappan seals are considered valuable historical sources mainly because:
options: They give clues about trade, beliefs, and the still-mysterious script
They are made of gold and are very expensive
They are the only objects ever found at Harappan sites
They contain fully translated messages about daily life
questions.hint: Seals are valuable because they give clues about trade, beliefs, and the still-undeciphered script, even though the writing cannot be read.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: Which of these was NOT commonly depicted on Harappan seals?
questions.hint: A ship with sails is not a commonly depicted image on Harappan seals, unlike animals and short lines of script.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: What does the presence of Harappan seals in Mesopotamia suggest to historians?
options: The Harappans and Mesopotamians never met
Mesopotamia is located in modern India
The Harappans likely had trade contact with Mesopotamia
Seals were invented in Mesopotamia and copied by the Harappans
questions.hint: Finding Harappan seals in Mesopotamia suggests that the Harappans likely had trade contact with that region.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: Which of these best explains why the meaning of Harappan seal symbols remains uncertain?
options: The symbols have already been fully explained in ancient books
The symbols are written in modern Hindi
There are no symbols on any Harappan seal
Historians cannot yet read the undeciphered Harappan script
questions.hint: The meaning of Harappan seal symbols remains uncertain mainly because the script has not yet been deciphered.

questions.subject: social-science

options: A unicorn-like animal with a single horn
questions.hint: This seal shows the unicorn-like animal, the single most common figure found on Harappan seals.

questions.question: This seal shows an animal with one long horn. What is this mysterious creature usually called by historians?
questions.hint: Historians usually call this mysterious single-horned figure the unicorn, even though no such real animal is known to have existed.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: Notice the small object placed in front of the animal on this seal. What is it usually believed to be?
options: A cooking pot for daily meals
A stand, possibly used for offerings
questions.hint: The small object in front of the unicorn figure is usually believed to be a stand, possibly connected to offerings or rituals.

questions.question: Seals like the one shown below were most likely used for what purpose?
options: Marking ownership of goods in trade
questions.hint: Seals like this were most likely pressed into clay to mark ownership of goods being traded.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: The row of marks above the animal on this seal represents which of these?
questions.hint: The row of marks above the animal figure represents the Harappan script, which has not yet been deciphered.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: Look at the seal shown below. Which animal is carved on it?
questions.hint: This seal shows a humped bull, recognizable by the raised hump on its back and the two curved horns.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: The animal on this seal has a raised bump on its back and a loose fold of skin under its neck. What are these features called?
questions.hint: The raised bump on the back is called a hump, and the loose skin under the neck is called a dewlap, both features of the humped bull.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: Which real animal, still commonly seen in India today, is shown on this seal?
questions.hint: The humped bull, also known as the zebu, is a real animal still commonly seen in India today.

questions.question: Which 19th century explorer had seen the ruins of Harappa but did not realize their true age and importance?

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: Why is the discovery of the Harappan Civilization considered so significant?
options: It proved that no ancient civilizations ever existed in South Asia
It had no real impact on how historians understood ancient India
It revealed a highly advanced ancient civilization that historians did not know about before
It showed that all ancient civilizations were exactly the same
questions.hint: The discovery was significant because it revealed a highly advanced ancient civilization that historians did not previously know about.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: Which of these best describes the extent of the Harappan Civilization?
options: It existed only in modern day China
It was limited to one street in one city
It covered only a single small village
It covered a very large area across present-day Pakistan and northwest India
questions.hint: The Harappan Civilization covered a very large area across present-day Pakistan and northwest India.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: Which of these is a proposed reason for the decline of the Harappan Civilization?
options: Changes in climate and the drying up of rivers
A sudden increase in modern factories
questions.hint: One proposed reason for the decline of the Harappan Civilization is changes in climate and the drying up of rivers.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: Which river is often mentioned in connection with theories about the decline of the Harappan Civilization due to drying up?
questions.hint: The Saraswati river is often mentioned in connection with theories about drying rivers and Harappan decline.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: Was the decline of the Harappan Civilization sudden or gradual, based on most evidence?
options: Gradual, with cities being abandoned slowly over time
It ended in a single afternoon
It never actually declined at all
questions.hint: Most evidence suggests the decline of the Harappan Civilization was gradual, with cities being abandoned slowly over time.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: Why do historians still debate the exact reasons for the decline of the Harappan Civilization?
options: The Harappans left detailed notes explaining the decline
Modern historians have stopped studying the topic completely
No single confirmed cause has been agreed upon by all historians
There is too much written evidence to sort through
questions.hint: Historians still debate the decline because no single confirmed cause has been agreed upon by all historians.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: Which of these is NOT considered a strong, confirmed reason for the Harappan decline today?
questions.hint: A sudden alien invasion is not a real or accepted theory. Climate change, trade decline, and river shifts are among the theories historians actually consider.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: Which of these theories about Harappan decline involves rivers changing course?
options: A change in the position of the moon
A sudden increase in modern population
Earthquakes or natural events shifting river paths
questions.hint: One theory suggests earthquakes or natural events shifted river paths, affecting Harappan settlements.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: Why might a decline in trade have affected Harappan cities?
options: Trade had no connection to city life
Cities never depended on trade at all
Trade only affected cities outside the Harappan region
Cities depended on trade for materials and resources they could not produce locally
questions.hint: Cities depended on trade for materials and resources that were not available locally, so a decline in trade could have serious effects.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: Which of these best describes how historians learn about the Harappan Civilization today?
options: By watching videos recorded at the time
By studying archaeological remains, since their script has not been deciphered
By interviewing people who lived through it
By reading detailed diaries written by the Harappans
questions.hint: Historians mainly learn about the Harappan Civilization by studying archaeological remains, since the script has not been deciphered.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: Why can historians not simply read Harappan records to learn about their government or religion?
options: Because all Harappan records were written in modern English
Because the Harappan script has not yet been deciphered
Because historians are not allowed to study ancient scripts
Because the Harappans never wrote anything at all
questions.hint: Historians cannot read Harappan records directly because the script has not yet been deciphered.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: Which type of age, based on the tools and metals used, does the Harappan Civilization belong to?
questions.hint: The Harappan Civilization belongs to the Bronze Age, based on the tools and metals they used.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: Roughly how long ago did the mature Harappan Civilization begin, if it started around 2600 BCE?
questions.hint: Since the mature Harappan Civilization began around 2600 BCE, that is roughly 4600 years ago from today.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: Which of these is true about the size of the Harappan Civilization compared to other ancient civilizations?
options: It was one of the largest in area among early civilizations
It was smaller than a single modern village
It had no cities of any kind
questions.hint: The Harappan Civilization was one of the largest in area among early civilizations.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: Which of these was an early, now largely questioned theory about why the Harappan Civilization declined?
options: Invasion by outside groups called Aryans
The discovery of new trade routes
A sudden increase in rainfall with no other effects
questions.hint: An early, now largely questioned theory suggested that invasion by outside groups, sometimes called Aryans, caused the Harappan decline.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: Why do modern historians treat the old invasion theory about Harappan decline with caution?
options: There is limited solid archaeological evidence to support it
No other theories about decline exist
All historians fully agree it is correct
It is proven completely true by strong evidence
questions.hint: Modern historians treat the old invasion theory with caution because there is limited solid archaeological evidence to support it.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: Which of these is the best description of how the Harappan Civilization ended?
options: Cities were gradually abandoned, likely due to a combination of factors
It ended in a single sudden battle
It ended because of a global pandemic recorded in detail
questions.hint: The Harappan Civilization likely ended gradually, with cities abandoned due to a combination of factors rather than one single event.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: Which of these would most likely help historians understand more about why the Harappans declined?
options: Refusing to study the topic further
Assuming the old invasion theory is completely correct
New archaeological evidence and further study of ancient climate and rivers
questions.hint: New archaeological evidence and further study of ancient climate and rivers would most likely help historians understand the Harappan decline better.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: Why is dating the Harappan Civilization sometimes given as 'about' a certain year rather than an exact date?
options: Because the Harappans wrote down the exact date themselves
Because dates from thousands of years ago are estimated using scientific methods and cannot always be pinpointed exactly
Because historians simply guess dates at random
Because exact dates are unimportant to historians
questions.hint: Dates from thousands of years ago are estimated using scientific methods, so they are often given as approximate rather than exact.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: Which of these methods do archaeologists use to estimate how old Harappan remains are?
options: Guessing based on the colour of the soil alone
Asking local residents for their opinion
Scientific dating methods applied to excavated materials
questions.hint: Archaeologists use scientific dating methods applied to excavated materials to estimate how old Harappan remains are.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: What do historians mean when they say the Harappan Civilization was 'urban'?
options: It existed only in modern cities today
It had no settlements of any kind
It had well-planned cities, unlike smaller village settlements
It was located entirely in forests with no buildings
questions.hint: Calling the Harappan Civilization urban means it had well-planned cities, rather than only small village settlements.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: Which of these statements about the Harappan Civilization is most accurate?
options: It was a simple civilization with no cities or planning
It was an advanced Bronze Age civilization with well-planned cities, though many aspects remain a mystery
Every detail about the Harappan Civilization is fully known and confirmed
It existed only in myths, with no real archaeological evidence
questions.hint: The Harappan Civilization was an advanced Bronze Age civilization with well-planned cities, though many aspects, like its script, remain a mystery.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: Why do you think the discovery of Harappan cities changed what historians believed about ancient India?
options: It proved that no ancient civilizations existed in India
It had no effect on historical understanding at all
It showed that ancient India had no connection to farming or trade
It showed that a highly organized urban civilization existed in the region thousands of years ago
questions.hint: The discovery showed that a highly organized urban civilization existed in the region thousands of years ago, changing earlier historical understanding.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: Which of these is an example of something that remains a mystery about the Harappan Civilization?
options: The exact meaning of their script and the nature of their government
The material most of their bricks were made from
The general location of their major cities
The fact that they used bronze tools
questions.hint: The exact meaning of the Harappan script and the nature of their government remain mysteries, unlike well established facts such as their brick material.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: What do most historians agree was a contributing factor, even if not the sole cause, of Harappan decline?
options: Environmental changes, such as shifts in rivers or climate
A worldwide shortage of modern electronics
questions.hint: Most historians agree that environmental changes, such as shifts in rivers or climate, were likely a contributing factor in the Harappan decline.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: Which of these best explains why studying the Harappan Civilization is considered exciting for historians?
options: Every single question about it has already been fully answered
Many questions about it are still unanswered, leaving room for new discoveries
It is considered a boring and unimportant topic
There is nothing left to discover about it
questions.hint: Studying the Harappan Civilization is exciting because many questions remain unanswered, leaving room for new discoveries.

questions.subject: social-science
questions.question: What overall lesson can be learned about historical research from the story of the Harappan discovery?
options: Ancient civilizations can never be studied without written records
Archaeology has no real value for understanding history
Historical research never leads to new discoveries
Even long-forgotten civilizations can be rediscovered through careful archaeological work
questions.hint: The story of the Harappan discovery shows that even long-forgotten civilizations can be rediscovered through careful archaeological work.
